title: APPROVAL OF FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE (FTZ) OPERATING AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND CALIFORNIA STEEL INDUSTRIES, INC., FTZ 202, SITE NO. 55

Summary
: Staff requests approval of a Foreign-Trade Zone (FTZ) Operating Agreement (Agreement) between the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) and California Steel Industries, Inc. (CSI), to operate its facility within FTZ 202, Site No. 55, located at 1400 San Bernardino Avenue, Fontana, CA 92335. Site No. 55 is a steel production facility, with warehouse and office building space totaling approximately 360.70 acres. Site No. 55 is located approximately 65 miles from the Port of Los Angeles (Port). CSI will operate its facility under FTZ procedures as a single-usage site. The proposed action is aligned directly with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets, Initiative 2: Increase the utilization of Port facilities and develop a plan to activate vacant port properties. FTZs are specifically designed to stimulate economic activity, utilize port property, and generate revenue. Approving developer and operator agreements directly activates port properties and designated zones, bringing in businesses that utilize the Port’s ecosystem. The proposed action also aligns with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure, and Sustainable Supply Chain, Initiative 1: Facilitate supply chain efficiencies and terminal velocity with stakeholders, with continuous enhancements to the Port Optimizer product. FTZs provide distinct operational and regulatory advantages that streamline how cargo moves through the logistics chain. They allow cargo operators to defer, reduce, or eliminate customs duties. This financial and administrative incentive attracts cargo volumes, reduces customs clearance delays, and improves overall supply chain velocity for Port stakeholders. The proposed Agreement is for a term of five years with three, five-year renewal options.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the proposed Foreign-Trade Zone Operating Agreement between the Harbor Department and CSI; 3) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to the proposed Foreign-Trade Zone Operating Agreement; and 4) adopt Resolution No. __________.
